ducktape for self-improvement

Outline of programs/docs/ducktape-for-self-improvement.md · J-177 · style after fluent31's SKILL.md: every section opens with a runnable example

An agent improves its own network on ducktape the way it improves anything: read what runs, change the code, test it natively, build the wasm, put it, schedule it, check it. This page is that loop, one runnable example per step.

Program vs view, side by side (§1)

tally: the program (every node, in consensus)
enum Op { Add { by: u64 } }
enum Query { Count }
static COUNT: Item<u64> = Item::new("count");

fn execute(op: Op) -> Result<()> {
    let Op::Add { by } = op;
    let count_after_add = COUNT.get()? + by;
    COUNT.set(&count_after_add)
}
tally-view: the view (one device, in the app)
let count = host.query(tally::ask::Count);
button("Add").on_click(|_, cx| {
    cx.ask::<Submit<tally::Tally>>(
        Op::Add { by: 1 });
});
cx.follow(tally::changes, reread_count);
ProgramView
runson every node, inside consensuson one device, in the app
holdsconsensus state (its key space)UI state, the device's store
entry pointsexecute(op), query(q)render, listeners
talksto other programs (query, emit, call)to programs only through the host
updatesprograms Set (state kept)SetView, or packed with its program

When to write which: a rule every node must agree on → program. Something one person sees or does → view. Neither, when a query plus a TOML covers it → a widget or a tool file.

Sections

  1. Head + read-first table
    the repo map, programs.md, roles.md, view README, sdk.md, tool-files.md, widgets.md, core found-a-network.md (this starts where that ends)
  2. A program and a view, side by side
    the tally pair above, real workspace crates so the doc can't rot
    no doc puts them side by side or says when to write which
  3. Priors that don't transfer
    Set swaps code under the same id · every key is replicated forever · interfaces only grow, retire by gap · no clock but env().time · a refusal undoes the frame · a view has no fetch, no timers · never hand-write an owner check
  4. The model in twelve lines
    programs, roles, accounts, frames, queries, blobs (code id = sha256), schedule, views, egress, harness
  5. Read what your network runs
    network_schema, one op's shape, programs Sources, Roster
    "which SDK commit matches what my network runs"
  6. Your first program, out of tree
    Cargo.toml by git at the Sources commit, patch lines, toolchain, cargo test
    programs.md only covers crates inside programs
  7. Test it natively (ABI-centric)
    MockHost: Add, then Count, then a refusal · MockChain: tally asks chat
  8. Your first view
    tally-view crate + TestAppContext: fake host answers Count, click Add, assert Submit
    how an out-of-tree view gets into the app
  9. Improve your own tools, with no code
    a tool file, a widget TOML (external tools after J-173)
  10. Build the wasm
    locked release build, pack, sha256 = code id; build on a machine with the pinned toolchain, yours or one your network registers in egress
    an out-of-tree packer (becomes ducktape pack, in this job)
  11. Ship it on your network
    put → schema-diff → Schedule Set → verify → roll back
    agent-only put path untested (proved here on a throwaway id) · where the notice is · no rollback recipe
  12. Take another network's release
    fetch by code id, check sha256, put, schema-diff, Set: an upstream fix without building it
    the whole section; no tool fetches another network's blob
  13. Exact signatures
    copy these; do not infer them
  14. Commands
    one block: test, clippy, builds, pack, sha256, schema-diff, blob put, op, query
  15. Traps
    Set lands no earlier than the notice · a put without a bundle isn't held · dirty checkout = no source stamp · no --locked = drifting bytes
  16. Where help lives
    the docs indexes and your network's own rooms
